top_stories.title: Over 41,000 DHS Employee Records Leaked Online
top_stories.summary: Over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employee records were leaked online after being allegedly stolen from an Okta single sign-on system. The breach exposed both personal and work information of DHS employees.

top_stories.title: DHS: 41,000+ Employee Records Leaked Online, Along With a Map of What Each Account Can Open
top_stories.summary: A threat actor published a database containing personal and work details of over 41,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees. The leaked data reportedly includes a map of what each employee account can access, exposing access control and authorization structures within DHS.

top_stories.title: Shufti ties AI agent actions to verified owners and permissions
top_stories.summary: Shufti has launched Know Your Agent (KYA), a verification solution designed to authenticate autonomous AI agents and bind their actions to verified human owners and defined permissions. The product addresses agentic identity challenges where AI agents perform transactions like opening accounts or moving funds, requiring businesses to verify agent authenticity, accountability, and authorization scope beyond simple access tokens.

top_stories.title: Fake IT help desk callers got by on little more than names and email addresses
top_stories.summary: Cisco Talos Incident Response documented multiple Q3 2026 engagements where attackers impersonated IT help desk staff via phone, email, and Microsoft Teams to trick employees into opening remote access sessions. Attackers used only employee names and email addresses to establish credibility, with at least one incident resulting in ransomware deployment.

top_stories.title: Attackers Chain Three Ivanti Connect Secure Flaws to Gain Unauthenticated Root Access
top_stories.summary: CISA added two Ivanti Connect Secure vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog after confirmed active exploitation in the wild. The flaws, including CVE-2026-111357 (CVSS 8.8), a missing authentication vulnerability, are being chained with a third flaw to achieve unauthenticated root access on affected systems.

news.title: Chainalysis Confirms Intrusion Into Internal Tools and Exposure of Customer Identity Data
news.summary: Chainalysis confirmed a cybersecurity incident in which an external actor accessed non-sensitive customer identity data through internal tools. The company stated that authentication credentials and session tokens were not compromised in the breach.

news.title: SS7 and Diameter Attacks: How Signaling Flaws Expose Your Phone
news.summary: SS7 and Diameter protocol vulnerabilities allow attackers to intercept SMS verification codes and track phone locations by exploiting trust relationships between mobile networks. The article, published by Cape mobile service, explains how these signaling flaws undermine SMS-based authentication and describes their security-focused mobile service as a defense.

news.title: CISA says max severity GitLab flaw now exploited in the wild
news.summary: CISA has reported that a maximum-severity GitLab vulnerability is now being actively exploited in the wild. The flaw relates to authentication bypass or account takeover capabilities in GitLab, making it directly relevant to identity and access management concerns.

news.title: Binance hit by $6.3 billion theft in what could be the biggest crypto heist on record
news.summary: Binance suffered a $6.3 billion cryptocurrency theft potentially involving a compromised DevOps engineer's laptop that allowed unauthorized access to a service container. The attacker used this access to submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions, with no evidence of a wallet private key leak found.

news.title: Okta jumps after-hours following tapped inclusion in the S&P 500
news.summary: Okta has been selected by S&P Dow Jones Indices to join the S&P 500 benchmark index. The announcement caused Okta shares to climb 2.1% in after-hours trading following the news.

news.title: Okta Set to Join S&P 500; Others to Join S&P MidCap 400 and S&P SmallCap 600
news.summary: Okta Inc. is set to join the S&P 500 index, moving up from the S&P MidCap 400, effective prior to the opening of trading on November 4. This index inclusion reflects Okta's market capitalization growth as a major identity and access management vendor.

news.title: Implement least-privilege access with designations in Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio
news.summary: Amazon SageMaker Unified Studio has introduced "designations," which are named permission sets enabling administrators to apply least-privilege access control at the project member level. The feature allows granular assignment of permissions within SageMaker's data and AI development environment.

news.title: $38.4 bn market cap: DHS Data leak details - Okta says its core systems not compromised | All you need about company
news.summary: A data leak allegedly exposing personal and job details of over 40,000 Department of Homeland Security employees is under investigation, with Distributed Denial of Secrets claiming the data came through Okta. Okta has stated it found no evidence that its core systems or infrastructure were compromised in connection with the incident.

news.title: Hackers steal and publish data on 41,000 Homeland Security workers
news.summary: A hacker group claims to have stolen and published data on 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees. The exposed data includes work contact details and internal group memberships, raising concerns about identity data exposure within a federal agency.

news.title: Hackers leak personnel data of 41,000+ Homeland Security staff, including ICE and border agents
news.summary: Hackers leaked personnel data of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees, including ICE and CBP agents. The breach involved staff details being published online, though the article description provides no specifics on the attack vector or identity systems involved.

news.title: 26,400 Valid Cloud and AI Credentials Found Exposed in Public Gitee Repositories
news.summary: Researcher Ben Zimmermann discovered 26,400 valid credentials exposed in public Gitee repositories after scanning 7.25 million public repos, reporting findings on October 28. The exposed credentials were primarily API keys for cloud and AI services, representing active authentication tokens that remained functional at time of discovery.

news.title: Hackers Publish Work Details of 41,000 Homeland Security Employees
news.summary: A hacktivist group has published work details—including names, titles, and phone numbers—of over 41,000 Department of Homeland Security employees. The data was reportedly extracted from a login system, raising questions about access controls and authentication security on government identity infrastructure.

news.title: Session security, token protection, continuous access evaluation, and measuring what users ACTUALLY sign in with
news.summary: This article is part five of a seven-part series on Microsoft Entra ID, covering session security, token protection, continuous access evaluation, and tracking authentication methods from MFA to passkeys. The piece examines how Entra ID manages tokens post-authentication and the security mechanisms used to protect ongoing sessions.

news.title: Massive data breach exposes 40,000 US Homeland Security employees
news.summary: A data breach has exposed sensitive information belonging to over 40,000 U.S. Department of Homeland Security employees. The compromised data includes details on officials in surveillance and human intelligence roles.

news.title: Trust Is Not What It Seems — and Fraudsters Are Counting on It
news.summary: The article examines how threat actors are bypassing technical security controls by using AI-assisted social engineering to manipulate help desks into granting unauthorized access. This attack vector directly targets identity verification and authentication processes at service desks, a core IAM control point.

news.title: Microsoft Plugs Nearly 1,000 Security Holes
news.summary: Microsoft released a record-breaking patch update addressing at least 974 security vulnerabilities across Windows and other software. Microsoft attributed the increased discovery rate partially to AI-assisted vulnerability detection, while security experts note organizations are struggling to keep pace with testing and deploying monthly fixes.
